evidence.excerpt: Common-source inductance (CSI) introduced by PCB interconnects degrades switching-speed and increases switching energy in GaN half-bridge circuits. This paper presents a parametric finite-element study of CSI as a function of five geometric variables: via diameter, via pitch, power-loop width, source-sense routing length, and copper pour layer count. Seventeen PCB variants were fabricated and CSI was measured by the impedance-analyser short-circuit method at 1 MHz. CSI ranged from 0.4 nH for a four-layer optimised layout to 3.1 nH for a two-layer reference layout. Switching-energy experiments confirmed that each additional 1 nH of CSI increased Eon by approximately 0.35 µJ at 15 A / 400 V. A design flowchart consolidating the parametric results is provided. Recommended design rules include a maximum source-sense trace length of 5 mm and a minimum of four vias per source return path. The findings apply to GaN devices in TO-leadless packages with source-sense pins.
